findings.issue: Excel data lookup fails because matchedTransaction.customer is a string (customer name), not an object. The OR operator always resolves to this truthy string and never falls through to matchedTransaction.customerData which contains the actual Excel data with _allDuplicates.
findings.consequence: customerObj becomes a string, customerObj._allDuplicates is undefined, no Excel fields are extracted, modal displays 'NO EXCEL FIELDS FOUND' error instead of showing Excel transaction details.
findings.correction: Change line 1219 to: const customerObj = matchedTransaction.customerData

findings.issue: Customer name lookup tries to access t.customer.name, but t.customer is a string (customer name), so t.customer.name is always undefined. Logic relies on fallback to t.customerName.
findings.consequence: Lookup works via fallback, but creates confusion and fragility. The logic incorrectly assumes customer might be an object with a name property.
findings.correction: Change line 1174 to: const tCustomerName = (t.customer || t.customerData?.name || t.customerName || '').toLowerCase().trim()
